title: Version numbers, vector clocks and merging field by field

videos.script:
Last lesson, a clock decided which edit to keep, and it was always the wrong question. {{question}} The real one is simpler. When the phone wrote, had it seen the tablet's write?

A version number answers that. {{version}} Every row carries one. A write says which version it read. If the server has moved on, it answers 409, and hands back what it has.

When there is no single server to count, a vector clock does the same job. {{clock}} One counter per device. Compare them, and you know whether two writes were in order, or concurrent.

Then comes the merge. {{merge}} Keep the version both devices started from, and look field by field. The phone changed the minutes. The tablet ticked it done. Both survive.

And once in a while, both changed the same field. {{ask}} That one goes to the person, with both values kept until they choose.
